moat_against: Undifferentiated commodity product — moat is location/reserves, no brand, network effects, or switching costs
Volumes hostage to construction cycles; revenue CAGR ~5.4% over 5y and ~0% over 3y on continuing basis
Reserves deplete; growth bought via M&A at rising per-ton prices (Premier, New Frontier, Lhoist $13.5B)
Q2 2026: record revenue but flat gross profit, operating earnings −10%, aggregates gross profit/ton −17% YoY
moat_for: Permitting scarcity — new greenfield quarries take years-to-decades of approvals; permitted reserves near growing metros are irreplaceable
Transport economics — aggregates uncompetitive beyond ~30–50 truck miles, so each deposit is a local oligopoly
Proven pricing power — FY2025 aggregates pricing +6.9%, Q2 2026 mix-adjusted organic pricing +3.7%, through-cycle increases
Public infrastructure is the largest end market and is funded multi-year; data-center/power demand adds support
Specialties (magnesia, lime via Lhoist) adds niche, higher-margin, less-cyclical revenue
moat_justification: Permitted aggregate reserves near growing metros are scarce and effectively irreplaceable, transport economics make each deposit a local oligopoly, and pricing power is proven through cycles (FY2025 aggregates pricing +6.9%; Q2 2026 mix-adjusted organic pricing +3.7%). The ceiling: the product is an undifferentiated commodity — the moat is location and reserves, not brand, network, or switching costs — volumes are hostage to construction cycles, and growth is increasingly bought via M&A at rising prices.
name: Martin Marietta Materials, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality local-monopoly aggregates franchise, moat 7/10, but at $472.39 (~37.5x TTM owner's earnings, 2.67% OE yield) it doesn't come close to the 15% hurdle — weighted IRR 6.1%, IV@15% $126.06; clears 15% only at ~$126, ~$95 with a margin of safety.
